Thessalonica 1403 was raised to confidence 2 and the 1431 event replaced by a 1423 loss to Venice at confidence 3.
Anatolian frontier of 718-724, 926 and 1111, the western Balkan lobe of 970-979, the Karaman plateau (1192) and Denizli and Paphlagonia (1202): shape changes with no page found.

After the 1204-1205 repair, 420 cells (106 k km2) of Cliopatria's 1202 shape still go to no state: Bulgaria 145, Turkey 118, Greece 67, North Macedonia 48, Kosovo 21, Albania 10. Probably Second Bulgarian Empire land (1185-1188) and inner Anatolia; not checked on a page.

Cyprus 653-960 (condominium) and its overlap with Cliopatria's Cyprus Condominium row; Africa 647-698; Palaiologan Anatolia 1305-1326; Thessaly's loss to Serbia in 1348 (no event); the Treaty of Gallipoli month. Pages Cyprus in the Middle Ages, Exarchate of Africa, Muslim conquest of the Maghreb, Byzantine Empire under the Palaiologos dynasty, Anatolian beyliks, Treaty of Gallipoli (1403) not opened.

Norman conquest of Apulia and Calabria 1041-1071, the Catepanate of Italy, Dalmatia and Raska 1000-1170 (pages Norman conquest of southern Italy, Catepanate of Italy, Theme of Dalmatia, Byzantine Empire under the Komnenos dynasty).

The reviewer's 'thin' list (17 items for a gap-filler) was not touched: inner Anatolia 1072-1085 (Sultanate of Rum), Edessa 944 (George Maniakes), Melitene 936 (John Kourkouas), Cyprus 960 (Cyprus in the Middle Ages), Cilicia 962 (Nikephoros II Phokas), Antioch 970 (Siege of Antioch 968-969), Balearics and Ceuta 718, Sevastopol 1016 (Georgius Tzul), Skopje 1010 (Battle of Skopje) and 1285 (Stefan Milutin), Cilicia 1139 (John II Komnenos), Sirmium 1188 (Bela III), Cyprus 1192 (Isaac Komnenos of Cyprus), Rhodes 1314 (Hospitaller conquest of Rhodes), Serbian conquests 1352 (Stefan Dusan), Serres 1385 (Serres).
